name: farcaster-mcp
description: Farcaster (social): me, publish_text, read_comments, reply_comment, read_mentions, delete, analytics

platform_mcp_farcaster_api_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_API_KEY
platform_mcp_farcaster_api_key.description: Neynar API key from https://dev.neynar.com: 'All API endpoints require an API key. Include the following header with every request: x-api-key' (https://docs.neynar.com/reference). Writes additionally need a signer (config field signer_uuid) created and approved for the same API key.

platform_mcp_farcaster_signer_uuid.title: PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_SIGNER_UUID
platform_mcp_farcaster_signer_uuid.description: UUID of an approved signer for the publishing account ('signer_uuid is paired with API key, can't use a uuid made with a different API key'; 'In order to post a cast signer_uuid must be approved', https://docs.neynar.com/reference/publish-cast). Required for publish_text, reply_comment and delete; env PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_SIGNER_UUID.

platform_mcp_farcaster_fid.title: PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_FID
platform_mcp_farcaster_fid.description: Farcaster id (integer) of the connected account, used by `me` (GET /v2/farcaster/user/bulk/?fids=) and read_mentions (GET /v2/farcaster/notifications/?fid=); env PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_FID.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /v2/farcaster/user/bulk/?fids=<fid> ('Comma separated list of FIDs, up to 100 at a time') returns BulkUsersResponse {users[{fid, username, display_name, custody_address, follower_count, following_count, profile{bio}, verifications, ...}]}; the connected account is account.users[0]. This verifies the API key and describes the configured fid; it does not prove the signer is approved.

tools.name: publish_text
tools.description: POST /v2/farcaster/cast/ {signer_uuid (required, 'UUID of the signer'), text, parent?} returns {success, cast{hash, author{fid}, text}}; `id` is the cast hash (0x-prefixed, used by read_comments / delete / analytics_post). `reply_to` is sent as `parent` ('parent URL of channel or hash of cast being replied to'), so it may be a cast hash or a channel URL; channel_id, embeds and idem are not sent. No url / created_at in the response.

tools.name: read_comments
tools.description: GET /v2/farcaster/cast/conversation/?identifier=<hash>&type=hash&reply_depth=1&limit=N ('Cast identifier (It's either a URL or a hash)'; reply_depth 0-5, default 2; limit 1-50, default 20; sort_type default chron) returns {conversation{cast{..., direct_replies[{hash, author{fid, username}, text, timestamp, direct_replies[]}]}, chronological_parent_casts}, next{cursor}}; `comments` are the direct replies. Pagination is cursor-based, so `page` is not sent.

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: A reply is a cast whose `parent` is the comment's hash ('parent URL of channel or hash of cast being replied to'); parent_author_fid is optional and not sent. Needs the approved signer_uuid.

tools.name: read_mentions
tools.description: GET /v2/farcaster/notifications/?fid=<configured fid>&type=mentions&limit=N (type is an array parameter of follows | recasts | likes | mentions | replies | quotes, sent as the single value mentions; limit 1-25, default 15) returns {unseen_notifications_count, notifications[{type, most_recent_timestamp, seen, cast{hash, author{username}, text, timestamp}}], next{cursor}}. Cursor pagination, so `page` and `since` are not sent. Neynar recommends webhooks for bot mentions ('It's more real time and cheaper compute').

tools.name: delete
tools.description: DELETE /v2/farcaster/cast/ with a JSON body {signer_uuid (required), target_hash (required, the cast hash)} returns {success, message} (the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}; the upstream body is under raw). 'In order to delete a cast signer_uuid must be approved', and the signer must belong to the cast's author.

tools.name: analytics_post
tools.description: GET /v2/farcaster/cast/?identifier=<hash>&type=hash returns CastResponse {cast{hash, author, text, timestamp, reactions{likes_count, recasts_count}, replies{count}, embeds, ...}}. The runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields (likes, recasts, replies).

tools.name: publish_image
tools.description: POST /v2/farcaster/cast/ {signer_uuid, text?, embeds: [{url}]}: `embeds` is an array with maxItems 2 of URL embeds ({url: string}) or cast embeds ({cast_id: {fid, hash}}), so the first TWO image_urls are sent as URL embeds and any further ones are ignored; Farcaster clients render image URLs inline. `id` is the cast hash; no url / created_at in the response. Needs the approved signer_uuid.
